subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should the disabled-delivery heartbeat path preserve `reason: "target-none"` and add an additive human-facing hint, or should OpenClaw rename the machine reason itself?
rationale: The code change is small, but the exposed heartbeat reason may already be consumed by scripts while an added hint becomes a new diagnostic payload surface.

options.title: Add an additive hint
options.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint to skipped heartbeat events, and render it in heartbeat/status output.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change the machine reason to a clearer value such as `delivery-disabled` and accept the compatibility risk for private consumers.

options.title: Leave current output
options.body: Keep the raw diagnostic unchanged and accept this as low-priority operator confusion.

recommendation.title: Add an additive hint
recommendation.body: Keep `reason: "target-none"`, add a disabled-delivery hint to skipped heartbeat events, and render it in heartbeat/status output.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the default-`none` heartbeat behavior and have the strongest current history on the affected heartbeat/status surfaces.
